findings.trigger: For a container with success_rate < 0.8, get_adaptive_timeout() first caps adaptive_timeout at self._config.max_timeout (line 157, comment 'Cap at maximum timeout'), then multiplies it by 1.5 (line 161). E.g. max_timeout=45000ms, a slow/flaky container's computed timeout gets capped to 45000 and then becomes 67500ms - above the documented maximum. The cap is not re-applied afterwards.
findings.suggestion: Apply the low-success-rate multiplier before the max_timeout cap (or re-clamp with min(..., max_timeout) after multiplying), so the returned value never exceeds config.max_timeout as the comment claims.

findings.trigger: is_donations_disabled() (line 39) and validate_donation_key() (line 58) only catch (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError, RuntimeError) around calls into services.config.config_service. The sibling file donation_config.py documents (lines 43-48) that config_service.save_config actually raises ConfigSaveError, a DDCBaseException - a type outside that tuple. If get_config_service()/validate_donation_key_service() can likewise raise a DDCBaseException subtype on a read failure, it would propagate uncaught out of these two 'compatibility functions' instead of being logged and turned into a safe False like every other error path here.
findings.suggestion: Either widen the except tuple to include the project's config-service exception base class (as donation_config.py now does with a broad, logged except), or confirm and comment that get_config_service()/validate_donation_key_service() never raise anything outside (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError, RuntimeError).
findings.unsure_why: services/config/config_service.py is not part of this review section, so it cannot be confirmed which exception types get_config_service()/validate_donation_key_service() actually raise on failure; the DDCBaseException precedent is only shown for save_config, a different method.

findings.trigger: check_and_retrieve_notification() reads the oldest waiting notification file, then tries notification_file.unlink(). If the unlink() call fails with OSError every time (e.g. wrong file ownership/permissions on the mounted config dir - the kind of permission mismatch this project has hit before), the method logs an ERROR and returns None (lines 74-79) but leaves the file in place. Because _waiting() always returns the oldest file first, every subsequent poll picks the SAME undeletable file, fails the same way, and returns None again - so no donation announcement is ever delivered again, even though newer notification files keep piling up behind it in the directory.
findings.suggestion: When delete fails, either move the file aside (e.g. rename to a .failed/.processed suffix) so later polls can reach the next file, or track already-returned files in memory so a stuck file does not block the whole queue forever.

findings.trigger: reset_donations() runs _backup_before_reset(), _clear_event_log(), _reset_sequence_counter(), _write_fresh_snapshot() inside one try block, but the except clauses only cover MechServiceError, (IOError, OSError), json.JSONDecodeError and (RuntimeError, AttributeError) (lines 68-103). _write_fresh_snapshot() calls into services.mech.progress_service (set_new_goal_for_next_level, member_count_for_goal, Snapshot, today_local_str) after the event log has already been truncated to '' by _clear_event_log(). If any of those calls raises a ValueError, TypeError or KeyError instead of one of the four handled exception families, reset_donations does not catch it: the exception propagates unhandled, past the point where the live event log is already empty, and the function never returns the graceful DonationResult(success=False, ...) the rest of the try/except is built to produce.
findings.suggestion: Widen the except coverage (or wrap the post-clear steps in their own try/except) so that any failure between _clear_event_log() and the successful write of the fresh snapshot is caught and reported the same way backup failures are - the live ledger being left empty with no valid new snapshot should never surface as an unhandled exception.
findings.unsure_why: services/mech/progress_service.py (set_new_goal_for_next_level, member_count_for_goal, Snapshot, today_local_str) is not part of this review section, so it cannot be confirmed whether any of these actually raise ValueError/TypeError/KeyError in practice, only that the except clauses here do not cover those types.

findings.trigger: delete_donation() reads the whole event log to compute deletion_counts and derives currently_deleted (line 347), then - outside any lock visible in this file - calls progress_service.delete_donation(target_seq) (line 358). Two overlapping delete/restore requests for the same donation (e.g. two admin tabs, or a double click that lands both requests before the first one's compensation event is written) could both read the same pre-click state, both pass the 'not already deleted'/'not already restored' guard, and both then call progress_service.delete_donation(), producing two DonationDeleted events for the same target_seq - which the toggle rule (odd count = deleted) turns back into 'not deleted', silently undoing the admin's delete.
findings.suggestion: Confirm that services.mech.progress_service.delete_donation() itself serializes concurrent calls for the same seq (e.g. via the same lock reset.py uses), or move the currently_deleted check inside that lock here.
findings.unsure_why: services/mech/progress_service.py's delete_donation() implementation is not part of this review section, so it is not known whether it applies its own locking/idempotency around the compensation event it writes.

notes: DonationStats.from_data (services/donation/donation_management_service.py:88, PLAN name #38) is never called from within this file - both get_donation_history and get_donation_stats build DonationStats via its normal constructor instead. Not reported as a finding (no behavioural trigger, may well be used by code outside this section), but flagged here since a reviewer might otherwise wonder why it looked unreachable. All five findings depend to varying degrees on code outside this section (services/config/config_service.py and services/mech/progress_service.py were not supplied); those dependencies are called out per-finding via certainty/unsure_why rather than guessed at.
